title: Differential pair + tail
description: The bare differential-pair transconductor sized by half-circuit: one input device at half the tail current, plus the tail source. Biased from the TAIL NODE and entered from the COMMON MODE, exactly like the 5T OTA: the pair's source sits at $V_{tail}$ (its body bias), its drain-source voltage is $V_{out} - V_{tail}$, and the tail device's drop IS the tail node — nothing iterated, no estimate to retune. The engine bisects $V_{tail}$ until the produced $CM_{in} = V_{tail} + V_{GS}$ equals the $CM_{dc}$ the application presents; sweep $CM_{dc}$ to trace the common-mode axis. The load is left abstract — a spec conductance gds_load_est (its inverse is the load resistance $R_L$) — so this sheet sizes the input stage independently of whatever mirror, resistor, or cascode terminates the drains. The common-mode gain and CMRR are estimate-grade (the tail output conductance sets them); a real CMRR also depends on drain-load and layout mismatch, so trust the sim for sign-off.

params.name: vos_target
params.note: input offset budget, 1 sigma; a bare half-micron pair at 20 uA sits near 7 mV with a generic Pelgrom coefficient

params.name: gds_load_est
params.note: conductance loading each drain; R_L = 1/gds_load_est. Set from the terminating load (mirror gds, resistor, or cascode)

params.name: CM_lo
params.note: input CM range, low edge — proven exactly by the cm-lo edge at every evaluation (the sweep put the widest closing range at 0.95-1.19 V on sky130 tt). The edge proves the ENDPOINT; the interior is the sweep's to show

params.name: CM_hi
params.note: input CM range, high edge — its ENDPOINT proven by the cm-hi edge

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: the input common mode the application presents. The engine places the tail node so the sheet sits exactly here; sweep it to trace the common-mode axis

params.name: V_out_dc
params.note: drain DC level; sets the input device vds

params.name: V_tail
params.note: the tail node — the one free bias variable, solved rather than set: the engine bisects between min and max (the BRACKET, not slider bounds) until the produced common mode equals CM_dc. The shown value is where it landed

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion: sets gm per current, noise, and the CM-low edge

params.name: gm_id_tail
params.note: tail inversion: higher V* costs CM-low headroom but tightens the current source

doc.title: Input-pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device at half the tail current. Its source sits at the tail node — that is its body bias — and its drain at V_out_dc, so its drain-source voltage is what is left between them.

doc.title: Tail current source
doc.description: The tail device carrying the full bias current; its saturation headroom sets the CM-low edge, and its output conductance sets the common-mode rejection.

rows.name: CM_in
rows.note: the input common mode this bias produces — an OUTPUT here, not a setting; rises monotonically with the tail node, so the pin is a well-posed bisection

rows.name: Gm
rows.note: differential-pair transconductance is the half-circuit gm

rows.name: Av
rows.note: half-circuit gain into the device gds in parallel with the load conductance

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: input-referred thermal density of the pair (both devices, hence the sqrt(2)); add the load's own contribution per the terminating device

rows.name: vos
rows.note: input-pair Pelgrom offset; the load pair adds in quadrature once its geometry is known

rows.name: Acm
rows.note: estimate: common-mode gain magnitude, set by the tail output conductance splitting between the two halves

rows.name: CMRR
rows.note: estimate: differential gain over common-mode gain; a real CMRR also depends on load and layout mismatch, so trust the sim

rows.name: tail_headroom
rows.note: how far the tail node sits above the tail device's saturation edge — exact, because the tail node is the variable rather than something inferred from a common mode

rules.note: below this the tail source drops out of saturation and the bias current collapses; the mechanism behind the low end of the common-mode range
the common mode this bias produces has to sit inside the range the application presents
paired with cm-not-below. Sweep CM_dc to see the whole span that closes
trips when the tail node is pushed so high the pair runs out of drain-source voltage at the drain DC level
estimate: a longer tail L (lower tail gds) lifts CMRR; sim owns the real number

edges.name: cm-lo
edges.note: the claimed low edge, proven exactly: the sheet re-evaluates at CM_dc = CM_lo with its own tail-node solve. Replaces the linearized reach estimate

edges.name: cm-hi
edges.note: the claimed high edge, proven the same way; the CM_dc sweep remains the authority on the full landscape
